clue.text: She might appear in dresses cut improperly

definitions.text: She might appear in dresses cut improperly

indicators.note: done improperly, the letters of the two words before it are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A temptress turns up wearing badly cut, perhaps revealing, dresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improperly' shuffles the letters of DRESSES CUT; the whole clue is also the definition, since a temptress might well be seen in a daringly cut dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A temptress who lures men is just the sort of woman who might wear a revealingly cut gown.

clue.text: Result of poor reception on TV for author

definitions.text: Result of poor reception on TV
definitions.meaning: the white speckle on an old analogue set with a weak signal
C. P. ..., the English novelist of Strangers and Brothers

explanation.surface: Bad television signal blamed on a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak signals give a speckled 'snow' picture on an analogue screen; C. P. Snow was an English novelist.

clue.text: Little girl's wedding presents

definitions.meaning: Dot, short for Dorothy, plus a possessive 's
a dot is a dowry, from French, property given on marriage

explanation.surface: A small daughter's gifts at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Dot is a pet name for a little girl, giving the possessive; a dot is also a dowry, the marriage portion a bride brings.

clue.text: Ordinary substance found in our old Republic

parts.note: ordinary means common, everyday
a person of substance has wealth

explanation.surface: Some everyday material is discovered inside an old state of ours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our old Republic' is England under Cromwell, 1649-60, officially called the Commonwealth.
explanation.definitionFit: The English republic of the Interregnum under Cromwell bore this name.

clue.text: Turpentine extract almost turning red

indicators.note: almost means the word for 'turning red' stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: rosing means becoming rosy, turning red

explanation.surface: A distillate from pine resin is nearly blushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the final G from ROSING, to rose being to flush pink or red.
explanation.definitionFit: The solid resin left after distilling turpentine from pine sap is what violinists rub on bows.

clue.text: Surmount unhappy experience with daily drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece surmounting another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: the Sun is a daily newspaper
a downer is a depressing experience

explanation.surface: Get over a miserable time with a drink each day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surmount' reads as 'overcome'; in a down entry it means the daily paper's name sits on top of the gloomy experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset, the evening tipple of colonial days.

clue.text: Removed a king of Mercia

parts.note: taken off means removed

explanation.surface: An old English ruler was deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the English Midlands; its eighth-century king built Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxon ruler who built the famous dyke along the Welsh border reigned there.

clue.text: Irish composer given hearing test, in practice

parts.note: John Field, Irish composer who invented the nocturne
a court hearing is a trial

explanation.surface: An Irish musician is auditioned for a practical exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' suggests sound, but it is a legal hearing, a TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A test carried out under real working conditions rather than in a laboratory.

clue.text: Redraft was revised later

indicators.note: revised means the letters of the two words before it are reworked

explanation.surface: The redraft was revised at a later stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges REDRAFT WAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean at a subsequent time.

clue.text: Making the best of work, boy and I celebrate

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
Tim, a boy's name
to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: A lad and I get the most out of our job and rejoice.
explanation.definitionFit: To optimise something is to make it as effective as possible.

clue.text: Such a strike shouldn't be beneath one

definitions.text: Such a strike shouldn't be beneath one

parts.words: Such a strike shouldn't be beneath one
parts.note: in boxing no punch may land below the strap round the waist; a 'strike' here is a blow, and the item named is a blow too

explanation.surface: Some industrial action is unworthy of a person.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a strike that is beneath one's dignity; it means a punch that must not land below the waistband, and belt is also slang for a hard blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit below the waist strap is a foul, and the same word is slang for a hard punch.

clue.text: Villain gets audience to wave

parts.note: a theatre's house is its audience
a breaker is a wave crashing on shore

explanation.surface: A scoundrel gets the crowd to wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar who forces his way into homes is a criminal.

clue.text: Head of organization creates procedural rule

parts.note: a point is a head, as of a spear
taken as written
order means organisation, tidy arrangement

explanation.surface: The boss of a company lays down rules of procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: In a meeting, a question raised about whether the proceedings follow the standing rules.

clue.text: Force to stop running

parts.note: a shore patrol whose job is to stop smugglers running contraband

explanation.surface: Compel someone to stop jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' looks like jogging, but it is smuggling, as in rum-running; 'Force' is a body of officers, not compulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: The service patrolling the shore once existed chiefly to stop smugglers landing goods.

clue.text: Blank cheque given to editor? How generous!

parts.note: a blank cheque gives a free hand

explanation.surface: An editor handed unlimited funds? How lavish!
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open-handed gives liberally and without stint.

clue.text: River Amazon?

parts.note: 'River' as one who rows, and 'Amazon' as a strong woman, not the South American waterway

explanation.surface: The great South American river.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'River' as one who rows a boat on a river and 'Amazon' as a powerful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A female rower is a strong woman propelling a boat on the water.

clue.text: Accident confused mechanics

indicators.note: confused means the letters of mechanics are jumbled

explanation.surface: Muddled mechanics cause a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad luck, an unfortunate event that happens by chance.

clue.text: Fine score has some maestri applauding

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Conductors clap a fine piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks musical beside 'maestri' but means a scratch or groove.
explanation.definitionFit: A stria is a thin groove or streak, a fine line scratched on a surface.

clue.text: He's stupidly taking a bishop back in place of queen

indicators.note: stupidly means the letters of the contraction are scrambled
back means the letter and the abbreviation before it are read in reverse order

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A fool moves his bishop back to where the queen should be on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' rearranges HES; 'back' turns A B into BA. The chess surface misleads: the queen is the biblical Queen of Sheba.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical queen who visited Solomon ruled this ancient land.

clue.text: Special bus for a road that takes one to beach

indicators.note: special suggests an unusual arrangement of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A special bus service on a road carries people to the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' signals rearranging three of the words; the abbreviation for road then closes the entry. The definition is the clue's tail, 'that takes one to beach'.
explanation.definitionFit: A board ridden on breaking waves carries a rider shorewards.

clue.text: Financial support city gives village

parts.note: a grant is financial support
Chester, a cathedral city in Cheshire

explanation.surface: Money from a city is given to a village.
explanation.walkthrough: Grantchester is a village near Cambridge, made famous by Rupert Brooke's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A small settlement beside the river Cam outside Cambridge.

clue.text: Deprived of coat, son gets cape

parts.note: Cape Horn, the southern tip of South America

explanation.surface: A boy without his overcoat is given a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a cloak, but it is a headland: Horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep that has had its fleece clipped is shorn.

clue.text: Do what's required sombrely? Nothing odd there

indicators.note: keeping nothing from the odd positions leaves only the even letters of the word

explanation.surface: Comply solemnly? There is nothing strange about that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing odd there' discards the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of SOMBRELY.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply with an order is to do as one is told.

clue.text: Political leader put in the tower

definitions.meaning: Sir Robert ..., British prime minister and founder of the police
a ... tower, a fortified keep in the Border country

explanation.surface: A party chief is locked in the Tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Peel was a Victorian prime minister; a pele or peel is a small fortified tower on the Scottish border.

clue.text: Decamp in two sections after this officer, to be more precise

definitions.text: Decamp in two sections after this officer, to be more precise

parts.words: Decamp in two sections after this officer, to be more precise
parts.note: split decamp into two parts and put them after the entry, and the full military title appears

explanation.surface: An officer is told to leave in two separate groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decamp' seems a verb, but it is a word split into DE and CAMP; placed after the four-letter entry it gives the full title aide-de-camp.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant officer serving a general is properly called an aide-de-camp.

clue.text: Knew Labour reform could be impractical

indicators.note: reform means the letters of the two words before it are re-formed

explanation.surface: Knew a reform of the Labour Party would never work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges KNEW LABOUR; Labour is a British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that cannot be made to work is not practicable.

clue.text: Satisfied with love? Not her!

parts.note: 'that did' means that was enough, satisfied
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Contented in romance? Certainly not this woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen of Carthage was abandoned by Aeneas and killed herself, so she was far from satisfied in love.
explanation.definitionFit: The tragic Carthaginian queen of Virgil's Aeneid died of a broken heart.

clue.text: Produce copper with splendid treatment plant

parts.note: a penny is a copper coin
royal treatment is splendid treatment

explanation.surface: Produce copper with a fine new process at a treatment plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment plant' looks like a works, but the plant is a herb of the mint family.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mint used in herbal medicine.
